result.title: Chain of Thought Monitoring Can Fail Even When CoT Is Necessary
result.summary: Chain of Thought (CoT) monitoring is used by frontier labs to detect misbehaviour of AI systems. Yet, its reliability remains poorly understood. We attribute this to the lack of a successful organizing principle that leads to generalizable conclusions about monitoring reliability in different regimes. Recent work attributes monitoring failures to the CoT not being necessary for the answer, and argues that CoT becomes monitorable when it is necessary. We show that this binary necessary/not-necessary organizing principle is too coarse by demonstrating that monitoring failures persist even if the CoT is necessary for the answer. In response, we introduce a more fine-grained organizing principle based on a hierarchy of four CoT necessity levels. Building on this hierarchy, we develop a framework for measuring CoT monitorability at the three lowest levels via intervention experiments. We demonstrate monitoring failures at all three of these levels on realistic, hard prediction tasks. On a difficult medical-diagnosis task, patient sex and a clinical attribute influence the answer in at least 19% and 24% of correct responses with a necessary CoT, respectively, yet their influence is almost never articulated. These results show that even when CoT is necessary, it is not guaranteed to be monitorable.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「CoT 对答案是否必要」细化为四级必要性层次，并在最低三层用干预实验测量 CoT 的可监控性，在困难医学诊断等任务上发现：即便 CoT 是必要的，仍存在关键属性（如患者性别、临床特征）影响答案却几乎不被表述的监控失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「必要性—可监控性」的干预式因果归因框架，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推理状态是否真正因果地贡献答案、以及轨迹监督与贡献分配的可靠性；但该工作为纯文本设定，与视觉多模态推理的迁移线索仍需人工确认。
